style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: An unbranded battery snow blower standing just inside an open garage at dusk, deep pine green housing, black discharge chute, one battery pack docked in its port, a second pack resting on the concrete floor beside it. A single warm worklight inside the garage rakes the machine from the left; beyond the open door a driveway runs out under a heavy slate sky with the first snowflakes falling. Wide anamorphic 35mm establishing shot, the machine sharp on the right third, weather filling the left with negative space, shallow depth of field, deep contact shadow under the wheels, palette of deep pine green, graphite and warm amber, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story turns on one decisive moment — the nine-day window closing as the first forecast turns — and the snow blower itself is the protagonist, so it must be the hero in its narrative context rather than a studio still. A dusk establishing shot inside the home's own garage carries both calendars at once: the machine lit and ready, the storm sky already arriving through the open door. Studio_object, the natural fit for a price story, is barred by the rotation rule, and the environment is what makes the availability tension legible.
cue: The snow-blower aisle has an expiry date this month.
subject: an unbranded teal battery snow blower with a docked battery pack standing inside an open garage as the first snowflakes reach the driveway
core_thesis: EGO's own site caps its snow-blower discount at $220, runs it only to November 30, and stamps it 'subject to availability' — so the price and the stock behind it can expire on different days, with a storm forecast as the tiebreaker.
core_conflict: A printed promotional deadline (up to $220, ending November 30) racing a weather-driven stock clock — the same nine days that expire the price can empty the shelf first.
composition: extreme asymmetry — the snow blower sharp on the right third inside the lit garage, the open door and storm sky filling the left two-thirds as negative space
